winner_analysis: Both winning agents (RegimeSwitcher +1473.5%, Patient +1250.1%) share three structural traits that explain their outperformance. First, extreme patience before the first purchase: RegimeSwitcher waited until 2018-12-06 (index=7.2, price=$3,509) and Patient until 2018-12-19 (index=3.55, price=$3,662). These dates sit within 2 weeks of Bitcoin's multi-year trough near $3,200, meaning both agents captured essentially the entire 2018-cycle recovery from near the absolute bottom. Second, DCA entry mechanics spread over 4-6 tranches at 14-21 day intervals smoothed execution across Dec 2018–Feb 2019 and again in mid-2022, reducing the cost basis risk of any single-day error. Third, high sell thresholds (75 and 78) meant neither agent ever exited their position during the entire 2017-2023 study window. The index apparently never sustained readings above 75 for long enough to trigger gradual sales. This buy-and-never-sell outcome was optimal in this specific period because the terminal price ($42,284 on 2023-12-31) was far above any exit price the agents would have received had they sold in late 2020 or early 2021. RegimeSwitcher's second buy in 2022 (index=10.5, price=$20,123, Jun-Jul tranches) compounded this advantage by adding BTC at a discounted price during the 2022 bear market, lowering the blended average cost basis even further.
loser_analysis: The four losing agents failed through two distinct mechanisms. Mechanism 1 — Premature entry (Technician and Fundamentalist): Technician's 2-day min_days_in_zone caused it to trigger on brief dips as early as 2018-03-28 ($7,949). BTC subsequently fell another ~60% to ~$3,200 over the next 9 months. Buying into a falling knife at $7,949 vs $3,500 means the cost basis was 2.3× higher than the winners', permanently capping returns. Fundamentalist (7-day minimum) bought first on 2018-08-17 — still 4 months before the real bottom and at prices roughly double the eventual trough. Mechanism 2 — Premature exit (Macro, Balanced, Fundamentalist): These agents had sell_threshold values of 70-72, which were triggered by the initial leg of the 2020-21 bull run. Macro sold Jan-Feb 2021 at $40,000-$52,000. BTC then reached $69,000 in November 2021, meaning Macro missed 33-73% of additional gain after selling. Balanced sold even earlier (Dec 2020) at $23,000-$28,000 — missing a subsequent 2.5× move. Fundamentalist sold in Dec 2020 ($26,000) and never re-entered before the 2022 bear market, so it held cash through the entire $26k→$69k run without participating. Technician's worst result (+160.6%) is explained by both problems simultaneously: early entry at a high cost basis AND a low sell threshold (70) that exited too soon. The combination is punishing because you overpay on the way in and underexit on the way up.
sell_signal_problem: The early-sell problem is the most analytically interesting finding. Agents with sell_threshold=70-72 correctly identified that the market was 'expensive' by historical standards in late 2020, but they were wrong about what that meant for future price action. The 2020-2021 cycle was unusual: the index crossed the 70-72 range during the initial parabolic leg (BTC ~$20,000-$40,000) but BTC continued to nearly double again to $69,000 before correcting. This reveals a structural flaw in the index model: euphoria-level readings can persist or even intensify for 6-12 months during a parabolic run. A threshold calibrated to 'historical tops' in a thinner, less institutional market (2017: ~$20k peak) will misfire when the next cycle's parabola goes higher and lasts longer. The winning agents' thresholds of 75-78 were never triggered at all during 2017-2023, which is ambiguous — it could mean the thresholds are well-calibrated for extreme tops (only 2021's $69k and 2024's runs would breach them), OR it could mean they are set so high they will never fire in any practical scenario, converting the agents into permanent holders. The evidence from this period cannot distinguish between these two interpretations. What is clear: threshold=70-72 exits too early in a parabolic regime, losing 33-170% of subsequent gains. A minimum threshold of 75 should be considered a lower bound for sell signals.
buy_threshold_finding: The evidence strongly supports buy_threshold in the range of 15-22 (score out of 100, where lower = more undervalued). RegimeSwitcher used threshold=22 and triggered at index=7.2 on 2018-12-06. Patient used threshold=15 and triggered at index=3.55 on 2018-12-19. Both triggered within 2 weeks of Bitcoin's multi-year trough, suggesting either threshold was low enough to catch the bottom without triggering prematurely. The critical insight is that these agents were NOT the first to trigger their buy signal — the index was already well below 22 for weeks before December. The min_days_in_zone filter (discussed separately) was the actual gating mechanism. Contrast with losing agents: Balanced (threshold=35) and Macro (threshold=30) triggered in April-August 2018 when index values were still above their thresholds but the price had not yet reached its true floor. This indicates that threshold=30+ is too high — it fires during the 'first leg down' of a bear market rather than waiting for genuine capitulation. The optimal buy threshold appears to be ≤22, with ≤20 being more conservative. A threshold near 15-18 is likely ideal: low enough to require genuine undervaluation (capitulation territory) while not so extreme it risks missing entries entirely in shallow bear markets.
min_days_finding: The min_days_in_zone parameter is arguably the single most important configuration variable in the experiment. Its effect is unambiguous: higher values produced dramatically better entry timing. The evidence by value: 2 days (Technician) → first buy March 2018, 9 months before bottom; 7 days (Fundamentalist) → first buy August 2018, 4 months before bottom; 18 days (RegimeSwitcher) → first buy December 2018, within 1 week of bottom; 28 days (Patient) → first buy December 2018, within 2 weeks of bottom. The mechanism is clear: a brief dip into undervalued territory is not the same as sustained capitulation. Short min_days values treat any temporary reading as a buy signal, catching falling-knife scenarios. The 18-28 day range required the index to remain below the buy threshold continuously for 2-4 weeks — a condition that was only met during genuine prolonged bear market bottoms. The difference between 18 and 28 days was negligible in outcome (both caught December 2018). This suggests the optimum is somewhere in the 18-30 day range: long enough to filter out temporary dips but not so long that entries are missed entirely. A value of 21 days (3 weeks) appears to be a practical optimum, sitting in the middle of the proven range. Values below 14 days appear unreliable based on this evidence.

model_improvements.change: Raise the minimum sell_threshold from 70-72 to 78-82, and add a secondary condition requiring the index to remain above the sell threshold for at least 14 consecutive days before initiating gradual exit
model_improvements.rationale: Agents with sell_threshold=70-72 exited at $23,000-$52,000 in late 2020 / early 2021, missing the subsequent move to $69,000. The 2020-21 cycle demonstrated that the index can sustain readings above 70 for extended periods during parabolic runs without the price having peaked. Adding a persistence filter (14+ days above threshold) before selling mirrors the proven logic of min_days_in_zone on the buy side — it separates genuine euphoric tops from temporary spikes
model_improvements.expected_impact: Would have kept Macro, Balanced, and Fundamentalist invested through the full 2021 run to $69,000, likely improving their final returns by 30-100% and pushing at least Macro and Balanced to alpha-positive territory

model_improvements.change: Set min_days_in_zone to 18-21 as the minimum viable value; deprecate any config below 14 days
model_improvements.rationale: Technician (2 days) and Fundamentalist (7 days) bought in March and August 2018 respectively — 4-9 months before Bitcoin's actual trough. Both cost-basis handicaps were never recovered over the study period. RegimeSwitcher (18 days) and Patient (28 days) both achieved near-perfect bottom timing in December 2018. The 18-21 day band appears to filter out transient dips while remaining reactive enough to catch sustained capitulation phases
model_improvements.expected_impact: Eliminates falling-knife entries. Technician's result of +160% would likely have improved to +800-1200% if it had waited for the December 2018 bottom instead of entering in March 2018

model_improvements.change: Add a 'cycle regime detector' that adjusts sell_threshold dynamically based on whether BTC is in an early bull, late bull, or bear regime — using on-chain velocity metrics (e.g., Puell Multiple trend direction, RHODL ratio slope) as regime signals
model_improvements.rationale: The sell_signal_problem revealed that a static threshold cannot differentiate between 'first leg up of a multi-year bull' (where selling is premature) and 'parabolic blowoff top' (where selling is correct). A regime-aware model could maintain a higher sell threshold during established uptrends (when parabolic continuation is more probable) and lower it once the on-chain metrics show deterioration of miner economics or long-term holder distribution
model_improvements.expected_impact: Would allow agents to hold through the $20k-$69k leg of 2021 (regime = confirmed bull) while still triggering exits at the actual top. Estimated improvement: captures an additional 30-100% of late-cycle gains that static-threshold agents sacrifice

model_improvements.change: Add a 'second-buy' rule: after the first DCA cycle completes, if the index drops back below buy_threshold × 0.7 within 24 months, initiate a second DCA cycle at 50% of the original allocation size
model_improvements.rationale: RegimeSwitcher made two successful buys: December 2018 (index=7.2) and June 2022 (index=10.5). Both catches were at deep undervaluation levels. The 2022 buy meaningfully reduced the average cost basis and compounded final returns. The current configs treat each cycle independently, but a programmatic rule that explicitly plans for a possible second capitulation event would systematize this behavior rather than leaving it to threshold coincidence
model_improvements.expected_impact: Adds a second allocation at deep value during bear markets that occur after initial positions are taken. In the 2017-2023 window, this captured the June 2022 bottom (~$20,000) — a price level that preceded a 100%+ recovery by end of 2023

model_improvements.change: Increase NUPL weighting to 0.28-0.32 and reduce Mayer Multiple weighting to 0.05-0.08 in the composite index formula
model_improvements.rationale: NUPL (Net Unrealized Profit/Loss) is the highest-weighted indicator in both winning configurations (0.24 for RegimeSwitcher, 0.28 for Patient). It directly measures the emotional/financial stress of the holder base — a fundamental driver of capitulation and euphoria. The Mayer Multiple (BTC price vs 200-day MA) is a price-only indicator that does not incorporate holder behavior and appears redundant given that MVRV and RHODL capture similar price-vs-cost dynamics more precisely. Reducing Mayer weight and increasing NUPL weight aligns the model more heavily with behavioral/on-chain fundamentals and less with technical price ratios
model_improvements.expected_impact: Improved index responsiveness to true capitulation events; reduced false signals from price momentum alone. Particularly beneficial in distinguishing late-bull corrections (NUPL still elevated, holders not stressed) from genuine bear market bottoms (NUPL near zero or negative)

key_insight: Patience on entry is worth far more than precision on exit. Both winning agents happened to never sell — but the foundational reason they won was that they waited 15-18 months from the start of the study period to make their first purchase, catching Bitcoin within 2 weeks of its multi-year low. The losing agents that entered 4-9 months too early (Technician, Fundamentalist) were permanently handicapped by their cost basis regardless of their exit logic. The min_days_in_zone parameter — specifically requiring 18+ consecutive days below the buy threshold — was the mechanical gating factor that separated the December 2018 bottom-buyers from the earlier falling-knife buyers. In a volatile, cyclical asset like Bitcoin, avoiding a premature entry is more important than timing a perfect exit: you cannot 'make up' a 2× cost basis disadvantage simply by holding longer.
